The workflow engine: the expression language a definition is written in, and the machinery that evaluates it. Depends on no dependency-injection container.
Retention sweeps for run history and superseded versions. In a cluster they run on one replica at a time, through the leader gate derived from the run lock.
The blocks every workflow host ends up writing: branches, loops, Try/Catch, conversions, arithmetic, JSON and an HTTP call. Opt-in, and any one of them is replaceable by name.
The workflow block SDK: what a block declares, what it is handed when it runs, and how a run is started. One dependency, so a block author's closure is one package.
The Redis half of a workflow cluster: the cluster-wide run budget, fire de-duplication, and the pub/sub transport every cross-replica signal travels on. Three seams, one connection, no schema.
The builder type the workflow library's add-on packages hang their AddX() methods on. One interface, one dependency.
Stepping a workflow run: sessions, breakpoints and snapshots. The machinery only — how a client reaches it, and how a paused run reaches a client, are the host's transport to choose.

The write side: the store that creates, updates, versions and publishes workflow definitions, and the HTTP surface over it. Nothing in the Executor references this package — a workflow written into the tables by something else is legitimate input to it.
Entity Framework Core persistence for the workflow engine: the nine tables it owns. Takes no dependency on TimescaleDB; running without it is supported.
The PostgreSQL half of a workflow cluster: the one-permit run lock over advisory locks, and the leader gate derived from it. One session per process, no schema, no migration.

The workflow engine's PostgreSQL schema: the library's own EF Core migrations, the history table that records them, and the TimescaleDB hypertable for the execution-step table. One call, AddPostgreSqlSchema(), after AddWorkflows; the host writes no migrations of its own. TimescaleDB is required.

The workflow HTTP surface as a minimal-API extension: MapWorkflowApi returns a RouteGroupBuilder the host mounts under its own policy. Separate from the engine so a host that runs workflows without exposing them takes no ASP.NET dependency.
